original.description: Studio portrait of Erich von Falkenhayn in the field-grey tunic of a Prussian general officer with gold shoulder cords, the Iron Cross 2nd Class ribbon in a buttonhole and the Iron Cross 1st Class on the breast; c. 1913 (Wikipedia dates the sitting to 1913; the Iron Cross 1914 suggests the print was taken or re-issued in 1914–15).
original.archive: Wikimedia Commons (retouched copy of a print also held by the Bundesarchiv, Bild 146-2004-0023)

colorization.status: ok — label 'colorized (AI-assisted)'; documented colours: field-grey (feldgrau) tunic with red piping, gold shoulder cords, black-and-white Iron Cross ribbon, silver-and-black Iron Cross 1st Class. Colour-check: the Iron Cross dates the decorations to August 1914 or later; if the sitting is 1913 the cross was added to the print or the date is 1914–15 — caption says 'c. 1913–14'.

caption: Erich von Falkenhayn (1861–1922), Prussian Minister of War from 1913 and, from 14 September 1914, Moltke's successor as Chief of the General Staff — the man who took the war to the Race to the Sea and Ypres. Colorized (AI-assisted) from a public-domain photograph by Albert Meyer, c. 1913–14.
credit: Original photograph: Albert Meyer, Berlin, c. 1913–14; public domain (via Wikimedia Commons; Bundesarchiv Bild 146-2004-0023). Colorization: Sandtable, AI-assisted, 2026.
notes: Provided by Dave 2026-08-22 (original: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erich_von_Falkenhayn). The Commons file is a retouched copy; Bundesarchiv Bild 146-2004-0023 is the un-retouched print. used_by is provisional until the beat exists — see cast.json for the 1914 placement.
